claim.pdf_says: FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL ( argument-1 )  -- both FUNCTION and TEST-NUMVAL are underlined in the printed general format (verified at 300 dpi crop).
claim.why_it_matters: The transcription marks FUNCTION as a required word but silently drops the underline on TEST-NUMVAL on the same line, so the file is internally inconsistent about which tokens the standard prints as required words. Compare 15.92.2 on page 955, which correctly renders '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME</u> ( argument-1 argument-2)'. No syntax is made illegal here (the function name is required regardless), but the marking loss defeats any tooling that reads <u> to recover required words.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED independently; every refutation angle was tried and failed.

(1) PDF glyphs, measured rather than eyeballed. Rendered page 956 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v956/spec_p956.png, 2550x3300) and scanned rows 960-1035 of the 15.93.2 general-format line for contiguous horizontal dark runs. Exactly one scanline qualifies -- y=1021 -- and it carries TWO separate runs: x in [273,471] (199 px) and x in [498,777] (280 px), separated by a ~27 px gap. The first sits under FUNCTION, the second under TEST-NUMVAL; the remaining ink to the right, '( argument-1 )', carries no rule at all. A 3x LANCZOS crop of (240,940)-(1200,1040) shows the same thing visually: two distinct rules, one per word, the second terminating at the final L of NUMVAL before the open paren. This cannot be read as one rule, a stray hyphen, or scanner noise. The claim's PDF quote is accurate.

(2) Markdown side, checked at the canonical source and not only in the extracted slice. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 38296 reads exactly '<u>FUNCTION</u> TEST-NUMVAL ( argument-1 )'. The extracted work unit page-956.md line 19 agrees, so the slice is faithful and the defect is in the canonical file. The claim's markdown quote is byte-accurate.

(3) Not reflow, page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation. The general format is a single unwrapped line in both sources; TEST-NUMVAL is present and correctly spelled, and the token is not split across lines. What is missing is only the <u> wrapper, on the same line. No 'Figure notes' annotation near line 38296 preserves the marking, so the information is simply gone.

(4) Not a house convention -- the strongest available refutation, and it fails on the file's own numbers. Of the 20 intrinsic-function general-format lines beginning '<u>FUNCTION</u>', 18 underline the function-name (counting line 35807, '<u>FUNCTION</u>  <u>HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC</u>', whose   does not affect the marking). Only 2 do not, and TEST-NUMVAL is one of them. The claim's control case verifies: line 38257 renders '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME</u> ( argument-1 argument-2)' with both words marked, one subclause earlier on the facing page.

(5) It does change meaning inside the transcription's own metalanguage, which is why this is not waived as pure formatting. ISO/IEC 1989:2023 5.2.2 Keywords: keywords 'are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats' and 'are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword'. 5.2.3 Optional words: optional words 'are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats' and 'may be written to add clarity'. As transcribed, 15.93.2 therefore asserts TEST-NUMVAL is an OPTIONAL word -- i.e. that 'FUNCTION ( argument-1 )' would be legal. No human reader would be misled, so cosmetic severity is right, but the file states something the printed standard does not.
verdict.corrected_description:
Real, and the claim is accurate as written -- both quoted strings are verbatim and the cited comparator checks out. Three refinements for the ledger.

(a) CITATION CORRECTION (supersedes an earlier verdict file for this page, which cited 5.2.4 and 5.2.5 -- both wrong). The governing subclauses are ISO/IEC 1989:2023 5.2.2 'Keywords' (uppercase + underlined = required) and 5.2.3 'Optional words' (uppercase, not underlined = may be written). 5.2.4 is 'Operands' and is unrelated.

(b) NUANCE ON 'why_it_matters'. The claim says 'no syntax is made illegal here', which is true, but the error runs the other way: per 5.2.2/5.2.3 the lost rule reclassifies TEST-NUMVAL from keyword to optional word, so the transcription makes a false PERMISSIVE assertion -- that the function-name may be omitted. Nothing legal is rejected; something illegal is implicitly licensed. Practical risk to a human reader is nil, so cosmetic severity stands, but this is why it is worth fixing rather than waiving.

(c) EVIDENCE AND FIX. The two PDF rules are mechanically confirmed at 300 dpi: the only ruled scanline on that line is y=1021, carrying runs x in [273,471] (FUNCTION) and x in [498,777] (TEST-NUMVAL), with '( argument-1 )' correctly unruled. Fix: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 38296 becomes '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-NUMVAL</u> ( argument-1 )'.

(d) PATTERN SWEEP (every bug is a pattern). TEST-NUMVAL is one of exactly 2 exceptions among the 20 '<u>FUNCTION</u>'-initial general formats. The other is specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34556, '<u>FUNCTION</u> CONVERT ( argument-1 source-format destination-format )', under anchor page-859. That sibling was NOT verified here -- its page was never rendered -- and is an unconfirmed suspect for the identical defect class; it should be checked with 'python scripts/spec/page_workunit.py 859' in the same pass before being fixed or dismissed.
